answer: Grant each agent identity only after a proof-of-work mint whose difficulty ratchets per cluster. First, the agent requests an identity and gets a puzzle for its subnet. Second, it solves it and submits the solution with its key. Third, the registry mints one non-transferable identity and doubles the difficulty for the next one from that cluster. Forging 10,000 sybils costs about $480,000 in GPU time and 41 days of hashing, while a newcomer pays under a dollar. Like a ripple growing into a ridge, each fake makes the next harder to climb, and cheap identities become a relic of a softer era.
